sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the unity of the Sukkah, which is an essential unity without division, and the unity of the Four Species, which is achieved by unifying diverse elements.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing the distinction between the Sukkah and the Four Species.
For although both indicate the matter of unity
(as will be explained below),
nevertheless there is a distinction between them.
For the unity of the Sukkah is an essential unity,
which has no
(from the outset)
division into details.
Therefore all of Israel are fit to sit in one Sukkah,
because the Sukkah is above division,
unlike the matter of the mitzvah of taking the Four Species, which is that from multiplicity unity is made.
For although they are four different species, from one extreme to the other,
as it is stated in the Midrash
that the Four Species of the Lulav correspond to the four types within Israel,
from the type corresponding to the Etrog, which has taste and smell
(Torah and good deeds)
to the type corresponding to the Willow, which has neither taste nor smell,
and they all become one bundle.
And also according to the interpretation
that the Four Species allude to the Holy One, blessed be He,
behold, from the fact that the matters above
(the Holy One, blessed be He)
are alluded to in the Four Species,
it is understood
that they are four different levels
[And according to the known principle that all interpretations of that same verse are connected to each other,
it can be said
that the distinction among the four levels above, which are alluded to in the Four Species, is from one extreme to the other,
similar to the distinction among the four types of Israel mentioned above],
and through the mitzvah of taking the Four Species
[for all four species are one mitzvah]
they become unified.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that after Sukkah and the Four Species comes the offering of the seventy bulls of the festival, which refines the seventy nations, and this is connected to the victory of Israel and the recitation of Hallel.

translations.translation: And behold, after the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah and the mitzvah of taking the Four Species, comes the mitzvah of offering the festival sacrifices,
the main part of which are the seventy bulls
[since the bull
(ox)
is the king among animals]
corresponding to the seventy nations.
For through the offering of the seventy bulls
[and likewise now through the recitation of the verses of the offerings of the seventy bulls,
and we will render [the] bulls [of] our lips],
the refinement of the nations is accomplished.
And it can be said
that the connection of the refinement of the nations through the offering of the seventy bulls to the mitzvah of taking the Four Species is,
for the ultimate perfection of the victory of Israel that is revealed through taking the Four Species
[for through Israel having their Lulavim and Etrogim in their hands, it is known that Israel are the victorious ones,
as above from the Midrash]
is,
that also the nations will agree to this,
and through the offering of the seventy bulls corresponding to the seventy nations, they are refined and purified, until they agree to the victory of Israel.
And this is also the connection of the recitation of Hallel during the seven days of Sukkot to the offering of the seventy bulls
[for that we complete the Hallel every day of the festival is because they are divided in their offerings],
for through the refinement and purification that is accomplished in the nations through the offering of the seventy bulls,
there is fulfilled "Praise Hashem, all nations; extol Him, all peoples, for His kindness has overwhelmed us,"
that the nations and peoples praise Hashem for this, that His kindness has overwhelmed us.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the praise of Hashem by the nations is a very lofty matter, completing the purpose of a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos in the lowest world, as understood from the concept of "Amen" unifying the names Havayah and Adnus.

translations.translation: And behold, that the nations and peoples praise and extol Hashem for this, that His kindness has overwhelmed us, is a very lofty matter.
To the extent that
(in a certain respect)
it is loftier than the matter of "His kindness has overwhelmed us" as it is in itself.
For through this
(that the nations praise, etc.)
the intention that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place for Himself in the lower worlds is completed,
in the lowest world, beneath which there is no lower.
And as is also understood from the maamar beginning "Baruch Tihiyeh Mikol HaAmim" of the Baal HaHilula,
for it is stated in the Yerushalmi,
"If a gentile blesses you, answer after him Amen," as it is said,
"Blessed shall you be from all the peoples."
And he brings in the maamar that it is stated in the writings of the AriZal
that "Amen" is the matter of the unification of Havayah and Adnus
[for this is that "Amen" in gematria equals Havayah Adnus].
And the explanation is,
that Havayah is the Essential Name
(the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above worlds),
and the name Adnus is, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,
"It is fitting for You to be called Adonai, for You are Master over all Your creations."
For in addition to this that the name Adnus is in the Sefirah of Malchus,
for Malchus is the root of the created beings,
behold, from the language of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, "You are Master over all Your creations"
(specifically "Your creations")
it implies that the name Adnus refers to these creations that are mere creations.
And through the unification of Havayah and Adnus,
that in Adnus shines Havayah,
so too is it done in the creations that come into being from the name Adnus
[including also these creations that are mere creations],
that the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above worlds, shines in them,
to the extent that they become a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
for Him, for His Essence.
And this is "If a gentile blesses you, answer after him Amen,"
for Israel are above worlds,
and through a gentile recognizing the superiority of Israel, to the extent that he blesses him,
this becomes a preparation and preface
for the unification of Havayah and Adnus,
and for a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower worlds.
